title: EmberPoint Q1 operational forecast + risk triage
summary: Quarterly check-in to align on Q1 forecast (usage, spend), reliability risks ahead of product launch, private deployment considerations and a pilot for dedicated capacity. Customer concerns: latency p95 for realtime flows, cost predictability, SOC2/KMS for PHI-adjacent data. Agreed to run a 2-week benchmark on Dedicated with sample traffic and follow up with pricing and security docs.
topics: Q1 usage forecast and burst planning
action_items: Maya Patel - send Dedicated pilot pricing matrix and burst cost projections - due 2026-01-12
Liam O'Connor - prepare benchmark plan and required artifacts (sample prompts, traffic profile, expected sequence lengths) - due 2026-01-11
Eric Dunn - share SOC2 and ISO documentation plus KMS/HSM integration notes - due 2026-01-10
Rajiv Menon - provide three week-of January windows for 2-week benchmark and attach sample request logs - due 2026-01-09
next_steps: Redwood to provision Dedicated pilot quote and bench plan
Customer to approve pilot window and share redacted logs
Schedule 2 hour technical runbook / deep dive after pilot kickoff
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-01-08 14:30 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Eric (Redwood CSM), Rajiv (EmberPoint), Sofia (EmberPoint), Jon (EmberPoint SRE), Tanya (EmberPoint Security), Mike (EmberPoint Finance)

Auto-summary (auto-gen may be rough): Quick Q1 forecast and risk triage focused on capacity forecasting and security for customer-facing realtime flows.

---- Transcript ----
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for coming on, I'm Maya, AE on the East Coast. We'll keep this tight, 45-ish min, goal is to align on Q1 usage, identify any reliability or security blockers before your launch, and agree next steps for a pilot. Quick intros?
[00:15] Rajiv: Hi, Rajiv here, Head of MLOps at EmberPoint. We're ramping up a realtime assistant feature, expecting spikes based on the A/B. We're a bit nervous about p95 latency and token cost.
[00:28] Sofia: Sofia, VP Product. We'll own launch timeline Q1 end. Need predictable cost and compliance checklist.
[00:36] Jon: Jon, SRE. I'm here for uptime and network constraints.
[00:40] Tanya: Tanya, security. I'll be validating SOC2, KMS, and data residency requirements.
[00:45] Mike: Mike from Finance, mainly to understand burn and committed capacity options.
[00:50] Liam: Liam, SE. I'll do the technical follow up and benchmarks.
[00:53] Eric: Eric, CSM, helping with operational onboarding.
[01:02] Maya: Great. Rajiv, can you give a short picture of current traffic and the forecast you showed in the deck last week? I'm thinking burst patterns and seq len distributions.
[01:10] Rajiv: Sure, so currently we're in beta with 3k monthly active users, roughly 500–700 rps at peak internal tests but real launch could push to 1.5k-2k rps for short bursts, about 10-15% sustained. Sequence lengths average 120 tokens but with tails up to 800–1k for long dialogs, which is where our cost gets scary becuase—sorry, because token multiplier. We also have KV cache on the client, but need server-side prefix caching too.
[01:42] Liam: Got it. That tail is important. On Redwood side we can recommend batching and prefix/KV caching to reduce per-token cost, but for realtime p95 we also want to avoid high batching delays. We can show the trade curve.
[01:56] Jon: On infra, we operate in AWS EKS across two regions, primary us-east-1 and failover eu-west-1. We'll want VPC peering and control plane connectivity—our security team insists no public internet for inference requests with PHI-ish payloads.
[02:12] Tanya: Correct, PHI-adjacent data means we'd prefer private deployment. But we also want the Redwood console for observability, so looking for a VPC private control plane option and KMS/HSM support.
[02:24] Maya: Understood. We have Redwood Private (sorry, sometimes the naming in transcripts is weird) that supports a private control plane and VPC connectors; also on-prem packages if needed. For KMS we integrate with customer KMS and bring-your-own keys to meet HSM requirements. Eric will share the security pack.
[02:41] Eric: I'll attach SOC2 docs, ISO summary, and our KMS integration notes after the call. Note: our private control plane has some setup lead time—usually 2–3 weeks.
[02:52] Mike: Finance question — what's the difference in unit economics between Hosted and Dedicated for us? At what commit level does Dedicated make sense?
[03:00] Liam: Very common Q. Hosted is pay-as-you-go with variable per-token pricing; Dedicated reserves GPU capacity so per-token can be much lower for sustained throughput. For your forecast with big burst windows, Dedicated plus autoscale burst could be cost-effective if you commit to at least 3 months of baseline. We'll run modelized numbers in the quote.
[03:19] Sofia: And latency? We need p95 under 350ms for short chats, and under 800ms for long sequences is tolerable.
[03:27] Liam: For p95 under 350ms, that depends on model choice and sequence length. For shorter sequences with a smaller model or quantized variant, Dedicated on A100-like or L4-equivalents hits that. For long sequences the KV cache + chunked responses help. We can benchmark with your actual prompt mix.
[03:46] Rajiv: We also want deterministic fallbacks. If primary capacity is saturated, we need auto-failover to a cheaper variant with lower latency degradation, not full errors. How mature is Redwood's routing/fallback?
[03:57] Maya: We have smart routing and automatic fallback policies—requests can be routed by latency or cost, with automatic fallback to compatible variants. We'll show configured routes in the pilot.
[04:08] Jon: When you say fallback, is the KV cache preserved across variants? Because losing cache will spike latency.
[04:15] Liam: Cache preservation depends on model family compatibility; if the model variant shares the same kv schema and tokenizer, we can reuse the cache. There are edge cases where tokenization differs and you lose cache. We'll document compatibility matrix in the runbook.
[04:30] Tanya: Security again — audit logs. We must have tamper-evident audit logs for all inference requests and admin changes, retention 7 years. Are logs stored in our account or Redwood's?
[04:42] Eric: For Private deployments logs can be pushed to your S3 or customer-managed logging. For Hosted we retain logs but we can export. We'll include retention and export options in the security pack.
[04:55] Rajiv: Cool. Next, pilot scope. We want a 2-week Dedicated pilot to simulate peak patterns with ~2k rps bursts and full-length tails. Can Redwood provision this fast?
[05:05] Liam: We can provision Dedicated pilot nodes quickly for 2-week runs, typically 48–72 hours to provision. Need redacted sample logs, model selection, and target SLOs.
[05:14] Maya: For the pilot we'll propose: baseline capacity for sustained 500 rps, scheduled burst to 2k rps, two model variants (high-quality and cost-optimized), enable KV caching, and measure p50/p95/p99 latency and cost per 1k tokens. Anything else?
[05:28] Sofia: Include error and fallback rates, and a failover simulation where primary region is throttled.
[05:35] Liam: We'll include canary deploy and region-failover simulation in the bench plan.
[05:40] Mike: Pricing—will ROI be shown? We need a comparison: current OpenAI spend projection vs Redwood Dedicated commit.
[05:47] Maya: We'll model it. We'll send a detailed pricing matrix and a conservative estimate for each scenario.
[05:52] Rajiv: On governance, we have a security review in two weeks with procurement. What's the lead time for Private? If setup is 2–3 weeks then we need to start immediately.
[06:01] Eric: Private setups require network validation and a joint runbook session—2–3 weeks is typical. For Dedicated pilot we can do an isolated Reserved pool without full Private setup to speed things up; that's often used to validate load and costs.
[06:12] Tanya: That sounds fine but procurement will need SOC2 + encryption details.
[06:17] Eric: Noted; I'll include that in the packet.
[06:21] [short silence, typing]
[06:30] Rajiv: A few gotchas from our side — long dialogs with 800–1k tokens sometimes lead to out-of-memory on our endpoints when batches pile up. We need to understand memory footprints per model.
[06:41] Liam: We'll provide memory figures and kernel selection notes; Redwood's runtime chooses kernels based on sequence length distribution and hardware. One caveat: quantized variants change memory patterns. We'll include per-model memory and perf numbers.
[06:54] Sofia: Also, do you support function calls and streaming while preserving cost accounting? Our front end streams partial replies and we need token-level cost attribution for analytics.
[07:05] Maya: Yes, streaming is supported and we provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns per request in the console. For privacy we can export event-level billing into your data lake.
[07:15] Jon: Network egress — if we keep control plane private but inference nodes in our VPC, egress will be inside region but still billed. Any tips for minimizing egress costs?
[07:23] Liam: Keep models and caching local to the VPC, use regional placement to avoid cross-region egress, and leverage prefix caching to reduce repeated tokenization overhead. We'll share a network placement guide.
[07:35] Mike: If we commit to a 6 month Dedicated contract, what's the typical SLA? We need 99.9% plus credits.
[07:42] Eric: Dedicated customers get SLA-backed uptime and latency objectives; specifics depend on the contract level. We'll include SLA templates in the packet.
[07:50] Rajiv: Let's talk escalation paths—if a production degradation happens during a launch week what's the expected Redwood response time?
[07:58] Maya: For Dedicated customers with premium support, initial response is <15 minutes for Sev1, on-call SE and SRE engagement within 1 hour, and a war room setup. We'll put the support ladder in the doc.
[08:10] Sofia: Request: can Redwood simulate a load test with a degraded region to validate graceful degradation?
[08:17] Liam: Yes, we can run a failover stress test as part of the pilot. We'll coordinate a window.
[08:22] Rajiv: Great. A couple of transcription notes from earlier pilots—sometimes token encoding differences cause small drift in outputs between model variants; for decisioning we need a consistent regression test harness. Do you have built-in eval support?
[08:35] Maya: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets/evals. We'll show an example eval harness. If you provide representative prompts we can run regression comparisons.
[08:46] Tanya: On compliance: can data be set to not be retained in logs? For PHI rules we need ephemeral request bodies but full audit metadata.
[08:54] Eric: Yes, we can redact sensitive fields at ingestion and still keep audit metadata. We'll propose a redaction pattern in the security docs.
[09:04] Rajiv: Perfect. Let's lock pilot dates—our preferred window is Jan 20–Feb 3. We can make the logs available by Jan 10.
[09:12] Maya: Rajiv, that works. We'll aim to have a pilot quote and bench plan to you by Jan 12 so you can sign off before Jan 20.
[09:19] Mike: One last finance check—if Dedicated pilot shows lower cost but throughput needs exceed baseline, are there burst add-ons?
[09:27] Liam: Yes, Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst capacity in the contract. We'll include burst pricing and a run-rate estimate per burst minute.
[09:36] Sofia: Okay, recap please?
[09:38] Maya: Quick recap: Redwood to send Dedicated pilot pricing and a benchmark plan (by Jan 12). Customer to share redacted logs and confirm pilot window (by Jan 10). Redwood to attach SOC2/ISO and KMS notes. After pilot kickoff schedule 2-hour technical deep dive. Action items captured in the doc.
[09:56] Rajiv: Thanks, that's clear. Any blockers from Redwood to starting the pilot?
[10:00] Liam: No blockers; just need the sample logs and model choices. Provisioning for pilot will be fast.
[10:06] Tanya: We'll look at the security pack and loop in procurement.
[10:10] Eric: I'll follow up with the packet and a proposed schedule.
[10:14] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll send notes and the quote.
[10:16] Sofia: Appreciate it, thanks.
[10:20] [call ends]

Notes on transcription fidelity: occasional mis-heard acronyms (K-V cash for KV cache), Redwood product names sometimes spaced (Red wood), and speaker overlap in the landing.

Referenced artifacts: "pilot-pricing-template.xlsx" (to be shared), "security-pack.pdf" (SOC2/ISO/KMS), "benchmark-plan.md" (will include traffic profiles).

End of transcript.
